title: The Second Part, or a Continuance of Poly-Olbion, from the Eighteenth Song
author: Michael Drayton
reason: The Thirtieth Song is a verse chorography of Westmorland and Cumberland, personifying Winandermere, Derwentwater and the Lakeland fells

title: An Essay towards a Natural History of Westmorland and Cumberland
author: Thomas Robinson
reason: The earliest sustained natural history of the Lake counties, covering the fells, minerals, springs and lakes of Westmorland and Cumberland

title: A Tour thro' the Whole Island of Great Britain, Divided into Circuits or Journeys (volume containing Letter X)
author: Daniel Defoe
reason: Contains Defoe's self-contained circuit through Westmorland and Cumberland, with Kendal, Cockermouth, Whitehaven and the 'unhospitable terror' of the fells

title: A Miscellany of Poems, consisting of Original Poems, Translations, Pastorals in the Cumberland Dialect
author: Josiah Relph
reason: The first collection of Cumberland dialect pastorals, written from the northern edge of the Lake District around Sebergham and Penrith

title: The Antiquities of Furness; or, an Account of the Royal Abbey of St Mary in the Vale of Nightshade
author: Thomas West
reason: Facsimile of the 1774 first edition; the standard antiquarian history of Furness, covering Furness Abbey, Cartmel, Coniston and the southern Lake District

title: An Excursion to the Lakes in Westmoreland and Cumberland, August 1773
author: William Hutchinson
reason: One of the earliest published Lake District tours, describing Windermere, Coniston, Derwentwater and Ullswater day by day

title: The Works of Thomas Gray in Prose and Verse, volume 3 (containing the Journal in the Lakes, 1769)
author: Thomas Gray
reason: Contains Gray's Journal in the Lakes, the 1769 day-by-day account of Keswick, Borrowdale and Skiddaw that shaped Lake tourism; text from the 1884 collected Works

title: The History and Antiquities of the Counties of Westmorland and Cumberland, volume 1
author: Joseph Nicolson
reason: Compiled with Richard Burn; the foundational parish-by-parish county history of Westmorland and Cumberland, covering the whole Lake District

title: A Guide to the Lakes, Dedicated to the Lovers of Landscape Studies
author: Thomas West
reason: The first true Lake District guidebook, setting out the celebrated 'stations' from which tourists should view each lake

title: Observations, Relative Chiefly to Picturesque Beauty, Made in the Year 1772, on Several Parts of England, Particularly the Mountains and Lakes of Cumberland and Westmoreland
author: William Gilpin
reason: The founding text of picturesque Lake District travel, devoted wholly to the mountains and lakes of Cumberland and Westmoreland

title: A Survey of the Lakes of Cumberland, Westmorland, and Lancashire
author: James Clarke
reason: A Penrith land surveyor's detailed survey of every Lake District lake with local history, customs and anecdote

title: The History of the County of Cumberland, and Some Places Adjacent, volume 1
author: William Hutchinson
reason: Comprehensive county history covering Keswick, Borrowdale, Derwentwater and the Cumberland fell parishes

title: A Journey Made in the Summer of 1794 through Holland and the Western Frontier of Germany, with a Return down the Rhine: to which are Added Observations during a Tour to the Lakes of Lancashire, Westmoreland, and Cumberland, volume 2
author: Ann Radcliffe
reason: The second volume contains Radcliffe's substantial self-contained tour of the Lakes of Lancashire, Westmoreland and Cumberland

title: A Fortnight's Ramble to the Lakes in Westmorland, Lancashire, and Cumberland
author: Joseph Budworth (Joseph Palmer)
reason: A pedestrian tour of the Lakes including the first published account of climbing Helvellyn and Great Gable

title: The Lakers: A Comic Opera in Three Acts
author: James Plumptre
reason: A satire on Lake District tourism, set among picturesque tourists at Keswick, Borrowdale and Skiddaw

title: A Companion and Useful Guide to the Beauties of Scotland, to the Lakes of Westmoreland, Cumberland, and Lancashire
author: Sarah Murray
reason: A pioneering woman traveller's practical guide with an extended section on the Lakes of Westmoreland, Cumberland and Lancashire

title: Britannia: or, a Chorographical Description of the Flourishing Kingdoms of England, Scotland and Ireland (Gough's edition, volume 3)
author: William Camden
reason: Volume three contains the full Cumberland and Westmorland chorographies, describing Winandermere, Derwentwater, Kendal and the mountain country

title: Letters from England, by Don Manuel Alvarez Espriella, volume 2
author: Robert Southey
reason: Contains Southey's extended fictionalised letters on the Lakes, with Keswick, Lodore, Skiddaw and Ambleside described at length

title: A Descriptive Tour, and Guide to the Lakes, Caves, Mountains, and Other Natural Curiosities in Cumberland, Westmoreland, Lancashire
author: John Housman
reason: A Cumberland-born writer's systematic descriptive guide to the lakes, caves and mountains of the three Lake counties

title: The Minstrel of the North; or, Cumbrian Legends: Being a Poetical Miscellany
author: John Stagg
reason: Verse legends of Cumberland by the blind Wigton poet, drawing on Eskdale, Keswick and Cumbrian folklore

title: The Bridal of Triermain; and Miscellaneous Poems
author: Walter Scott
reason: Text from a later collected printing of a verse romance set at Triermain, Threlkeld and the Vale of St John in Cumberland, with Lakeland landscape throughout

title: The Excursion, being a Portion of The Recluse: A Poem
author: William Wordsworth
reason: Wordsworth's long philosophical poem set entirely in Lake District valleys, churchyards and fells around Grasmere and Langdale

title: Fragments, in Prose and Verse, by Miss Elizabeth Smith, with some Account of her Life and Character
author: Elizabeth Smith
reason: Letters and journal fragments written during the author's residence at Patterdale and Coniston, with detailed Lakeland description

title: The Tourist's New Guide, containing a Description of the Lakes, Mountains, and Scenery in Cumberland, Westmorland, and Lancashire
author: William Green
reason: A resident Ambleside artist's two-volume descriptive guide to the whole Lake District

title: Tours to the British Mountains, with the Descriptive Poems of Lowther and Emont Vale
author: Thomas Wilkinson
reason: A Quaker Penrith writer's mountain tours centred on Helvellyn, Langdale, Borrowdale and the Cumberland fells

title: A Concise Description of the English Lakes and Adjacent Mountains
author: Jonathan Otley
reason: The Keswick guide-writer's compact description of the lakes with the first sound account of Lake District geology

title: A Guide through the District of the Lakes in the North of England, with a Description of the Scenery, &c. for the Use of Tourists and Residents
author: William Wordsworth
reason: Wordsworth's own prose guide to the Lake District, the classic statement of its landscape, society and conservation

title: Ballads in the Cumberland Dialect, with Notes Descriptive of the Manners of the Peasantry
author: Robert Anderson
reason: The classic Cumberland dialect ballads, recording fell-country speech, fairs, weddings and customs

title: A Complete Guide to the Lakes, comprising Minute Directions for the Tourist, with Mr Wordsworth's Description of the Scenery of the Country and Three Letters upon the Geology of the Lake District
author: John Hudson
reason: Edited with Adam Sedgwick; combines a Kendal tourist guide, Wordsworth's Description and Sedgwick's three letters on Lake District geology

title: Recreations of Christopher North, volume 2
author: John Wilson
reason: Contains Wilson's Lake District essays and rambles around Windermere, Rydal and Elleray where he lived

title: The Poetical Works of Miss Susanna Blamire, 'The Muse of Cumberland'
author: Susanna Blamire
reason: Collected poems and Cumberland dialect songs by the 'Muse of Cumberland', rooted in the Caldbeck fells and Carlisle plain

title: The Scenery and Poetry of the English Lakes: A Summer Ramble
author: Charles Mackay
reason: A summer ramble through the Lake District interwoven with the poetry the region generated

title: Homes and Haunts of the Most Eminent British Poets, volume 2
author: William Howitt
reason: Contains extended chapters on Wordsworth at Rydal and Grasmere and on Southey and Coleridge at Keswick

title: The Old Man; or, Ravings and Ramblings round Conistone
author: Alexander Craig Gibson
reason: Rambles round Coniston Old Man by a Lakeland doctor, with fell-walking, mining and local character sketches

title: Half a Life-Time Ago
author: Elizabeth Gaskell
reason: A tale set wholly among the Westmorland fells and farms above Coniston and Langdale

title: A Complete Guide to the English Lakes
author: Harriet Martineau
reason: The standard guide by a resident of Ambleside, combining topography with Lake District society and economy

title: The Northmen in Cumberland and Westmoreland
author: Robert Ferguson
reason: An antiquarian study of Norse settlement and place-names throughout the Lake District valleys

title: The Lazy Tour of Two Idle Apprentices
author: Charles Dickens
reason: Written with Wilkie Collins; opens with a sustained comic account of the ascent of Carrock Fell in Cumberland in driving rain

title: Cumberland and Westmorland, Ancient and Modern: The People, Dialect, Superstitions and Customs
author: Jeremiah Sullivan
reason: A Kendal writer's account of the people, dialect, superstitions and customs of the Lake counties

title: The Half-Brothers
author: Elizabeth Gaskell
reason: A tale set entirely on the Cumberland fells, whose climax is a fatal snowstorm on the high fell above the family farm

title: The History and Topography of the Counties of Cumberland and Westmorland
author: William Whellan
reason: An exhaustive directory-history of every parish in Cumberland and Westmorland, including all the Lake District valleys

title: The Annals of Kendal: being a Historical and Descriptive Account of Kendal and the Neighbourhood
author: Cornelius Nicholson
reason: History of Kendal and its Westmorland hinterland, the traditional gateway town to the Lake District

title: Recollections of the Lakes and the Lake Poets: Coleridge, Wordsworth, and Southey
author: Thomas De Quincey
reason: De Quincey's memoir of his years at Dove Cottage and of Lakeland life among the Lake Poets

title: The Lake Country
author: Eliza Lynn Linton
reason: A Cumberland-born writer's valley-by-valley account of Lake District landscape, people and traditions

title: Lizzie Lorton of Greyrigg: A Novel
author: Eliza Lynn Linton
reason: A novel of Cumberland fell and coastal village life, drawing on the author's Crosthwaite childhood near Keswick

title: The Worthies of Cumberland, volume 1
author: Henry Lonsdale
reason: Collective biography of notable Cumbrians, with lives rooted in Keswick, Cockermouth and the Lakeland fells

title: The Folk-Speech of Cumberland and Some Districts Adjacent
author: Alexander Craig Gibson
reason: Dialect stories and rhymes recording the speech and folklife of Cumberland and the Lake District valleys

title: On the Drifts of the West and South Borders of the Lake District, and on the Three Great Granite Dispersions
author: Daniel Mackintosh
reason: A field survey of glacial drifts and erratic dispersion around the western and southern margins of the Lake District

title: Annales Caermoelenses, or Annals of Cartmel
author: James Stockdale
reason: A detailed history of Cartmel and its priory in the southern Lake District, with Windermere and Furness material

title: Lays and Legends of the English Lake Country, with Copious Notes
author: John Pagen White
reason: A verse collection dedicated entirely to Lake District legends, places and traditions, with topographical notes

title: Memoir and Letters of Sara Coleridge, volume 2
author: Sara Coleridge
reason: Letters and reminiscences of her Greta Hall childhood at Keswick and of the Wordsworths at Rydal and Grasmere

title: Lady Anna
author: Anthony Trollope
reason: A substantial part of the novel is set in and around Keswick and the Cumberland lakes

title: Recollections of a Tour Made in Scotland, A.D. 1803
author: Dorothy Wordsworth
reason: The tour begins and ends in the Lake District, with sustained description of Keswick, Grasmere and the passage out of Cumberland

title: Autobiography of Mrs Fletcher, with Letters and Other Family Memorials
author: Eliza Fletcher
reason: The memoir of a long resident of Lancrigg, Grasmere, recording Lake District society, Wordsworth's circle and daily life

title: The Geology of the Northern Part of the English Lake District (Memoirs of the Geological Survey, Quarter Sheet 101 S.E.)
author: James Clifton Ward
reason: The official Geological Survey memoir for the Skiddaw, Derwentwater and Borrowdale country

title: Cumbriana; or, Fragments of Cumbrian Life
author: William Dickinson
reason: A West Cumberland farmer's record of Lakeland customs, sports, farming and dialect

title: Harriet Martineau's Autobiography, volume 2
author: Harriet Martineau
reason: Records her years at The Knoll, Ambleside, with extended accounts of Lake District neighbours and social life

title: Tourists' Guide to the English Lake District
author: Henry Irwin Jenkinson
reason: A detailed late-Victorian walking and touring guide to the whole Lake District

title: The Thorough Guide to the English Lake District
author: Mountford John Byrde Baddeley
reason: The most authoritative late-Victorian route guide to Lake District fells, passes and valleys

title: The Shadow of a Crime: A Cumbrian Romance
author: Hall Caine
reason: A historical novel set in Borrowdale and the Newlands fells above Derwentwater

title: A Flora of the English Lake District
author: John Gilbert Baker
reason: The first systematic flora of the Lake District, mapping plant distribution across its fells and lakes

title: Hortus Inclusus: Messages from the Wood to the Garden
author: John Ruskin
reason: Letters written from Brantwood to the Beever sisters at Coniston, closely observing Lake District weather and landscape

title: Through England on a Side Saddle in the Time of William and Mary
author: Celia Fiennes
reason: Her 1698 northern journey includes a self-contained passage through Kendal, Windermere, Ullswater and Cumberland, the earliest woman's account of the region

title: Robert Elsmere
author: Mary Augusta Ward
reason: Opens with an extended Westmorland sequence in 'Long Whindale', a thinly disguised Lake District valley near Ullswater

title: Praeterita: Outlines of Scenes and Thoughts Perhaps Worthy of Memory in My Past Life
author: John Ruskin
reason: Text from the 1899 issue; includes sustained passages on Ruskin's Keswick and Derwentwater childhood and his later life at Brantwood on Coniston Water

title: A History of Cumberland
author: Richard Saul Ferguson
reason: A scholarly county history of Cumberland covering the Lake District fells, valleys and market towns

title: Letters of John Keats to His Family and Friends
author: John Keats
reason: Contains the run of letters from Keats's 1818 northern walking tour describing Windermere, Ambleside, Helvellyn and Skiddaw

title: Tales and Legends of the English Lakes
author: Wilson Armistead
reason: A collection of legends and traditions attached to named Lake District lakes, fells and villages

title: A Vertebrate Fauna of Lakeland, including Cumberland and Westmorland with Lancashire North of the Sands
author: Hugh Alexander Macpherson
reason: The standard Victorian faunal survey of Lakeland, recording birds and mammals fell by fell and lake by lake

title: Literary Associations of the English Lakes, volume 2
author: Hardwicke Drummond Rawnsley
reason: A Keswick vicar's survey of the writers associated with each part of the Lake District

title: Climbing in the British Isles, volume 1: England
author: Walter Parry Haskett Smith
reason: The first British rock-climbing guide, whose largest section catalogues Lake District crags and gullies

title: Anima Poetae: from the Unpublished Note-books of Samuel Taylor Coleridge
author: Samuel Taylor Coleridge
reason: Notebook entries from Coleridge's Greta Hall years, including his celebrated Scafell and Borrowdale fell-walking observations

title: Thorstein of the Mere: A Saga of the Northmen in Lakeland
author: William Gershom Collingwood
reason: A historical novel of Norse settlement set on Coniston Water and the Furness fells

title: Journals of Dorothy Wordsworth, volume 1
author: Dorothy Wordsworth
reason: The Grasmere journal, a day-by-day record of life, weather and walking in the Lake District between 1800 and 1803

title: Rock-Climbing in the English Lake District
author: Owen Glynne Jones
reason: Text of the posthumous third edition (1900) of the foundational Lake District climbing guide, describing routes on Scafell, Pillar, Gable and Great End

title: The Book of Coniston
author: William Gershom Collingwood
reason: A history and description of Coniston, Torver and the surrounding Lake District fells

title: Lakeland Words: A Collection of Dialect Words and Phrases as Used in Cumberland and Westmorland
author: Bryham Kirkby
reason: A glossary and dialect sketches recording the everyday speech of Lake District farms and villages

title: Helbeck of Bannisdale, volume 1
author: Mary Augusta Ward
reason: Set at a Westmorland manor in the Lake District fell country, with landscape integral to the novel

title: Bygone Cumberland and Westmorland
author: Daniel Scott
reason: Antiquarian essays on the history, customs and legends of the Lake counties

title: Life and Nature at the English Lakes
author: Hardwicke Drummond Rawnsley
reason: Essays on Lake District birds, weather, shepherds and fell life by a resident Keswick clergyman
